Roasted Red Pepper Dip

By Jeeca / October 8, 2026 at 7:04 am
Share Facebook X Pinterest

Smoky, creamy, and nutty Roasted Red Pepper Dip with roasted garlic, pumpkin seeds, gochujang, and lemon juice. Perfect with pita.

Jump to Recipe

  1. Why You'll Love This Roasted Red Pepper Dip Recipe
  2. THE INSPIRATION FOR THIS RED PEPPER DIP
  3. HOW TO MAKE THIS ROASTED RED PEPPER DIP

This Roasted Red Pepper Dip Recipe is so flavorful. It's smoky, creamy, and nutty. It's packed with fire-roasted red bell peppers, roasted garlic, roasted pumpkin seeds, gochujang, lemon juice, maple syrup, and a little egg-free Kewpie mayo for a rich dip with a really nice savory heat.

I love roasting the peppers over an open flame or gas stove because you get that smoky, charred flavor before blending everything together. The pumpkin seeds add body and nuttiness, while the roasted garlic makes the dip sweet, mellow, and aromatic.

This dip is packed full of flavor and is great as, of course, a dip with bread or pita (see my homemade recipe here), crackers, and vegetables, but you can also use it as a spread for sandwiches, wraps, grain bowls, and even as a pasta sauce! This recipe is really extremely versatile. Feel free to adjust the gochujang depending on your desired heat.

Why You'll Love This Roasted Red Pepper Dip Recipe

  • Made with fresh red bell peppers roasted until charred and tender.
  • Packed with smoky, creamy, and nutty flavors from roasted peppers, garlic, and pumpkin seeds.
  • The gochujang adds a savory kick and a little heat.
  • Blends into a smooth, rich dip in the food processor.
  • Great for serving with bread, crackers, vegetables, sandwiches, wraps, and bowls.

THE INSPIRATION FOR THIS RED PEPPER DIP

I love a good roasted pepper dip because the peppers become so sweet and smoky once charred. After peeling off the skins and removing the seeds, the peppers blend into this bright, flavorful base that's perfect with roasted garlic.

For this version, I knew I had to add roasted pumpkin seeds for body and gochujang for a little savory heat. It gives the dip a deeper flavor while still keeping it fresh from the lemon juice and herbs on top.

ROASTED PEPPER, GARLIC, AND PUMPKIN SEEDS

  • red bell pepper roasted, peeled, and seeded
  • garlic, roasted
  • Olive oil and salt
  • pepitas or hulled pumpkin seeds 
  • Olive oil

DIP

  • olive oil
  • gochujang adjust to desired heat
  • Kewpie mayo, or egg-free version, or vegan mayo of choice
  • lemon juice
  • maple syrup

GARNISH

  • Olive oil
  • Smoked paprika
  • Chopped chives
  • Thin chiffonade fresh mint leaves

TO SERVE

  • Pita - homemade pita recipe here
  • Crackers
  • Vegetable sticks
  • Sandwiches wraps, or grain bowls
  • As pasta sauce!

HOW TO MAKE THIS ROASTED RED PEPPER DIP

PREPARE THE BELL PEPPER AND PUMPKIN SEEDS

  • Roast the red bell peppers over an open fire or gas stove flame, turning as needed, until charred all over and tender.
  • Transfer the roasted peppers to a bowl and cover. Let them steam for 10-15 minutes, or until cool enough to handle. This helps loosen the skins.
  • Peel off the skins and remove the charred bits and seeds. You can use a paring knife to carefully scrape off the seeds and skins. Avoid rinsing the peppers if possible so you keep more of that smoky roasted flavor.

BLEND THE DIP

  • Add the roasted and seeded peppers, roasted garlic cloves, roasted pumpkin seeds, olive oil, gochujang, egg-free Kewpie mayo, lemon juice, and maple syrup to a food processor.
  • Process for 5-6 minutes, scraping down the sides as needed, until smooth and creamy. Taste the dip and feel free to season with more salt, lemon juice, maple syrup, or gochujang, to taste, if needed.

SERVE AND ENJOY

  • Transfer the dip to a serving bowl. Drizzle with olive oil, then garnish with smoked paprika, chopped chives, and thin chiffonade mint leaves.
  • Serve with bread, pita (homemade pita recipe here), crackers, vegetable sticks, or anything of your choice.
  • Enjoy!

Roasted Red Pepper Dip

No ratings yet
This Roasted Red Pepper Dip Recipe is smoky, creamy, and nutty. It's packed with fire-roasted red bell peppers, roasted garlic, roasted pumpkin seeds, gochujang, lemon juice, maple syrup, and a little egg-free Kewpie mayo for a rich dip with a really nice savory heat.
Print Recipe Pin this Recipe Rate this Recipe
Prep Time 25 minutes mins
Cook Time 15 minutes mins
Total Time 40 minutes mins
Course Appetizer, Dips, Sauces, Side Dish, Sides, Snack, Snacks, Starters
Cuisine American, Fusion, Italian, Lebanese, Middle Eastern, Western
Servings 4 servings
Calories 181 kcal

Ingredients
 
 

ROASTED PEPPER, GARLIC, AND PUMPKIN SEEDS

  • 1 lb fresh red bell pepper roasted, peeled, and seeded (see notes)
  • 1 head garlic roasted
  • Olive oil and salt for the roasted garlic
  • 1/2 cup pepitas or hulled pumpkin seeds, 65 g
  • Olive oil for the seeds

DIP

  • 1 tbsp olive oil
  • 1 tbsp gochujang adjust to desired heat
  • 1 tbsp Kewpie mayo egg-free version, or vegan mayo of choice
  • 2 tbsp lemon juice
  • 1/2 tbsp maple syrup

GARNISH

  • Olive oil for drizzling
  • Smoked paprika
  • Chopped chives
  • Thin chiffonade mint leaves

TO SERVE

  • Pita homemade pita recipe here
  • Crackers
  • Vegetable sticks
  • Sandwiches wraps, or grain bowls

Instructions
 

ROAST THE GARLIC & PUMPKIN SEEDS

  • Preheat the oven to 350F/180C. Slice the top off the garlic head to expose the cloves, then drizzle with olive oil and season with a pinch of salt.
  • Wrap the garlic in foil and roast for 35-45 minutes, or until the cloves are soft, golden, and easy to squeeze out. Set aside until cool enough to handle.
  • For the pepitas/hulled pumpkin seeds, place these on a parchment paper-lined baking tray. Drizzle some oil to coat the seeds. Bake at 350F/180 for 8-10 minutes, stirring the seeds, or until they start to smell nutty and are golden brown.

ROAST THE PEPPERS

  • Roast the red bell peppers over an open fire or gas stove flame, turning as needed, until charred all over and tender.
  • Transfer the roasted peppers to a bowl and cover. Let them steam for 10-15 minutes, or until cool enough to handle. This helps loosen the skins.
  • Peel off the skins and remove the charred bits and seeds. You can use a paring knife to carefully scrape off the seeds and skins. Avoid rinsing the peppers if possible so you keep more of that smoky roasted flavor.

BLEND THE DIP

  • Add the roasted and seeded peppers, roasted garlic cloves, roasted pumpkin seeds, olive oil, gochujang, egg-free Kewpie mayo, lemon juice, and maple syrup to a food processor.
  • Process for 5-6 minutes, scraping down the sides as needed, until smooth and creamy. Taste the dip and feel free to season with more salt, lemon juice, maple syrup, or gochujang, to taste, if needed.

SERVE AND ENJOY

  • Transfer the dip to a serving bowl. Drizzle with olive oil, then garnish with smoked paprika, chopped chives, and thin chiffonade mint leaves.
  • Serve with bread, pita (homemade pita recipe here), crackers, vegetable sticks, or anything of your choice.
  • Enjoy!

Notes

RED PEPPER

  • I personally prefer roasting my own peppers since I find that some bottled ones have a slightly bitter taste, but if you'd like you can use bottled roasted red peppers (I like the ones from Divina).
  • If you aren't able to roast the peppers in open fire, roasting these peppers in the oven or in a broiler at a very high temperature of 200C or higher to get the skins nice and blistered would be the next best option.
